title: Employer-side discovery survey
source: docs/framework-research/06-employer-side-discovery-research-plan.md §3 with the eight [WF] additions and the pilot-only closing items (12-instrument-change-log.md rows 1 to 8 and 11). Transcribed 2026-11-08.

sections.title: Your role in hiring
sections.intro: Four questions that route the rest of the survey. Nothing here identifies you beyond your account.

items.prompt: In the last 24 months, which best describes your role in hiring?
options: Hiring manager (I own the role and decide)

items.prompt: Roughly how many roles have you been involved in hiring for in the last 24 months?
What kinds of roles, mostly? Select all that apply.
Organisation size, in employees.

sections.title: In your own words
sections.intro: Two open questions before any list is shown, so the list does not put words in your mouth.

items.prompt: Think of the last role that was hard to fill. In a sentence or two, what made it hard?
If you could fix one thing about how your organisation screens applicants, what would it be?

sections.title: The problems
sections.intro: A list of problems people report with hiring. Pick the ones that cause you the most difficulty in your own work.

items.prompt: Select up to 5 that cause you the most difficulty in your own work.
options: Too many applications to review properly
Most applicants appear unqualified on the surface
Hard to tell real capability from keyword-optimised or AI-written résumés
The people doing the first screen don't have the domain knowledge to judge technical or specialised experience
Hiring managers reject most of the candidates screening passes through (interviews that go nowhere)
Strong candidates get missed because their titles, tools or wording don't match the posting
Roles close unfilled or have to be reposted
Candidates stop responding or drop out part-way
Poor candidate experience damages our reputation
Job descriptions are inaccurate, out of date, or wish lists
The hiring manager and the recruiter disagree about what the role actually needs
We don't find out whether our hires worked out, so screening never improves
Compliance or bias risk from screening tools and criteria
Salary or level mismatch discovered late in the process
Interviews are inconsistent from one interviewer to the next
Working-style or team fit can't be assessed until very late
Our ATS or screening tools are rigid or hard to configure
I can't explain or justify a screening decision when asked

items.prompt: Of the ones you selected, which single problem would you fix first?
For each problem you selected: how often does it occur, and when it does, how costly is it?
Anything missing from the list?

sections.title: How screening actually happens
sections.intro: Facts about your process. If you do not know a number, say so; that is itself an answer.

items.prompt: Who does the first review of applications for a typical role?
Does your process use required keywords, knockout questions or auto-reject rules before a human looks?
Typical applications per role.
Of the candidates the first screen passes, roughly what share does the hiring manager decline without an interview?
items.note: [WF] required in both branches; sets whether C-14 is a decision point

items.prompt: Do you track whether hires are performing or still employed at 90 days or one year, and link it back to how they were screened?
How often have you later learned that a strong person was screened out before you saw them?
How confident are you that your first screen does not eliminate people who could do the job?
What gives you that confidence?
When a requisition or a candidate is put on hold, what usually happens to it?
options: Comes back on a planned date
Comes back only if someone pushes
items.note: [WF] sets the priority of the hold-state requirement

sections.title: A screening tool
sections.intro: A screening tool that breaks the job description into individual requirements and, for each candidate, shows whether each requirement is met, which document or statement is the evidence, a one-sentence reason, and a coverage score computed from those verdicts. Reviewers can see every judgment and overrule any of them.

items.prompt: How useful would this be in your work?
What would make you trust a verdict enough to act on it? Select all that apply.
options: Knowing the hiring manager can audit it
Knowing it was tested on past hires

items.prompt: What would make you overrule a verdict?
How much time per application would you accept spending with such a record?
Biggest concern about a tool like this?

sections.title: Before you go
sections.intro: Two yes-or-no questions. Your email is already on your account, so there is nothing to type.

items.prompt: Would you be willing to do a 30-minute follow-up conversation?
Would you like the summarised results when they exist?

sections.title: About the survey itself
sections.intro: Pilot only. These two questions are about the survey you just took, not about hiring.

items.prompt: Roughly how long did that take, in minutes?
Which question did you most want to skip?
